title: Preparation reaches the counting configuration
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $a$ be a state of $M$, and let $w$ and $s$ be Boolean words. There exist a natural number $t\le 2(|s|+1)$ such that, after $t+1$ steps, the split-body machine started in its preparation state with $s$ on its first work tape and all other work tapes blank, on input $w$, is in the counting configuration initialized with the simulated machine in state $a$, the auxiliary tape storing $s$, and empty output. At every time from $0$ through $t+1$, its state is not the anchor state.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
The preparation configuration has $s$ on the first work tape and empty tapes elsewhere
